title: Final Revision and Assessment
description: Last-mile checklists, the mock examination, and entry to the final exam, completion and certification.
objectives: Pass the mock examination under real conditions
Enter the final examination ready and calm

topics.title: Final Checklists
topics.description: Every must-know definition, equation and diagram in one place.

lessons.title: Definitions and Equations Master List
lessons.description: The 20 definitions and 4 equations no candidate may fumble.
objectives: Write all 20 definitions word-perfect from memory
Write all 4 equations with correct direction
lessons.introduction: Examiners cannot mark what they cannot recognise. These definitions and equations are the currency of every biology paper — mint them now.

contents.title: Twenty definitions
contents.body: Cover the right column; recall; check. (1) Diffusion — net movement of particles from high to low concentration down a gradient. (2) Osmosis — net movement of water from high to low water concentration across a partially permeable membrane. (3) Active transport — movement against a gradient using ATP and carriers. (4) Enzyme — specific protein catalyst with an active site, unchanged by reaction. (5) Denaturation — irreversible loss of 3D shape (heat/extreme pH) destroying function. (6) Photosynthesis — CO2 + water → glucose + oxygen using light and chlorophyll. (7) Aerobic respiration — glucose + oxygen → CO2 + water + large energy. (8) Gene — DNA section coding one trait. (9) Allele — one version of a gene. (10) Genotype — allele pair carried; phenotype — trait expressed. (11) Mitosis — one division → 2 identical diploid cells (growth/repair). (12) Meiosis — two divisions → 4 unique haploid cells (gametes). (13) Natural selection — variation + competition + differential survival + inheritance shifting allele frequencies. (14) Species — interbreeding group producing fertile offspring. (15) Ecosystem — community plus non-living environment. (16) Trophic level — feeding step from producers. (17) Homeostasis — maintaining constant internal conditions by negative feedback. (18) Reflex — fast involuntary response via receptor→sensory→relay→motor→effector. (19) Transpiration — water loss from leaves driving xylem pull. (20) Germination — sprouting requiring water + oxygen + warmth.

contents.title: Four equations, zero confusion
contents.body: PHOTOSYNTHESIS: 6CO2 + 6H2O →(light/chlorophyll) C6H12O6 + 6O2. AEROBIC RESPIRATION: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy (~30 ATP). ANAEROBIC (muscle): glucose → lactic acid + small energy. ANAEROBIC (yeast): glucose → ethanol + CO2 + small energy. Direction discipline: photosynthesis BUILDS glucose (needs input); respiration BREAKS it (releases output). Common swap: writing respiration's arrow for photosynthesis — check every equation's direction before moving on. Word equations earn full marks where symbols are not demanded; add symbols only when confident.

contents.title: Worked example: the 10-minute self-test
contents.body: Method: fold paper in half. Left: numbers 1–20. Without notes, write each definition from the titles alone (diffusion, osmosis, ...). Time: 10 minutes. Marking: exact = tick; close = half; missing/wrong = cross. Score under 16: re-learn crosses using Module 11's chain technique, sleep, re-test tomorrow (spaced repetition beats cramming). Score 16+: attempt the 4 equations blind, then diagrams (next lesson). Repeat daily until 20/20 twice running — mastery is consecutive perfection, not one lucky pass.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
20 definitions + 4 equations = the paper's currency.
Osmosis names the membrane; active transport names ATP; enzymes name the active site.
Photosynthesis builds; respiration breaks — never swap arrows.
Mastery = 20/20 twice running, spaced over days.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Definitions decide marks: precise terms, named structures, stated conditions. Drill them spaced and blind until perfect is routine.

lessons.title: Diagrams You Must Draw
lessons.description: The six most-examined diagrams and how to reproduce each for full marks.
objectives: Draw and label six key diagrams from memory
Annotate diagrams with functions, not just names
lessons.introduction: A perfect diagram can earn 6 marks in 3 minutes — the best rate in the paper. These six appear year after year.

contents.title: The six diagrams
contents.body: (1) PLANT CELL: wall, membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole, chloroplast, mitochondrion — rectangular with even walls. (2) ANIMAL CELL: membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondrion — rounded, NO wall/vacuole/chloroplasts. (3) HEART (double circulation): four chambers, aorta/vena cava/pulmonary vessels, valves, arrows showing flow + O2 colours. (4) LEAF SECTION: cuticle, upper epidermis, palisade, spongy + air spaces, lower epidermis with stomata/guard cells, vein (xylem above, phloem below). (5) FLOWER (half-section): sepals, petals, anther/filament, stigma/style/ovary/ovule. (6) REFLEX ARC: receptor → sensory → spinal cord relay → motor → muscle, with CNS box and direction arrows. RULES (Module 10): large, sharp pencil, single lines, no shading, ruled touching labels, title + magnification. Annotate ONE function per label where space allows ('xylem — carries water up').

contents.title: Worked example: the heart in 3 minutes
contents.body: Drill: draw the heart from memory, timed. Minute 1 — outline: two atria (top, thin walls), two ventricles (bottom, left wall THICK), septum dividing. Minute 2 — vessels: aorta arching from left ventricle, vena cava entering right atrium, pulmonary artery leaving right ventricle, pulmonary veins entering left atrium. Minute 3 — valves (dots + labels: bicuspid, tricuspid, semilunars) + flow arrows + title 'Vertical section of the mammalian heart'. Self-mark: 1 per correct chamber, vessel pair, valve set, arrows, title. Under 5: redraw immediately — motor memory builds through repetition, not reading.

contents.title: Watch: Cell Organelles Review (rapid self-test)
contents.body: Replay 'Cell Organelles and Structures Review' by the Amoeba Sisters (official channel stream) — shout each structure's name BEFORE the reveal, then sketch the cell it belongs to.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
Six diagrams: plant cell, animal cell, heart, leaf section, flower, reflex arc.
Draw timed (3 min each); self-mark against label checklists.
Annotate functions, not just names, where space allows.
Motor memory comes from redrawing, never from rereading.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Six diagrams, three minutes each, drawn blind and marked harshly. Diagrams are the fastest marks in biology — bank them.

topics.title: Mock Examination
topics.description: Sit the full mock under real conditions, review it ruthlessly, then enter the final.
objectives: Convert mock misses into final-exam readiness

lessons.title: Sitting the Mock
lessons.description: Exam-day simulation: conditions, conduct and the module mock examination.
objectives: Reproduce real exam conditions for the mock
Apply timing and command-word discipline throughout
Score at least 60% to unlock final-exam entry confidence
lessons.introduction: This is the dress rehearsal: 10 questions, 40 minutes, no notes, no pauses. Treat it as the final and the final will feel familiar.

contents.title: Mock protocol
contents.body: CONDITIONS: quiet room, clear desk, timer set to 40 minutes, phone OFF and away, water only. CONDUCT: attempt the module assessment below in ONE sitting, in order, showing working for calculations; mark-and-move past 3-minute stalls; use remaining time to review flagged questions only. FORBIDDEN: notes, videos, re-reading lessons mid-mock, extra time ('just 5 more minutes' invalidates the rehearsal). SCORING: 60%+ = proceed to the final exam (Topic 2, Lesson 2); 50–59% = repair misses (assignment) then re-sit once; below 50% = return to weakest modules (Module 11 clinic) before re-sitting. HONESTY WARNING: inflating a mock score only relocates failure to the final — the mock is a measuring instrument, and cheating breaks the instrument.

contents.title: Worked example: post-mock triage
contents.body: A student scores 7/10, missing Q3 (nitrogen bacteria), Q6 (heart trace), Q9 (leaf starch logic). TRIAGE: Q3 = knowledge gap → re-study Module 7 Lesson 2.1 (bacteria names) + flashcards. Q6 = retrieval gap → redraw the heart 3x timed (Lesson 2 drill). Q9 = reasoning gap → re-read Module 9's destarch logic + write the conclusion pattern 5x. REPAIR TIME: 45 minutes total, weakest first. RE-TEST: re-attempt all three blind tomorrow. RULE: every miss gets a named repair within 24 hours — misses without repairs repeat in the final.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
Mock = 40 min, one sitting, no notes, no extra time.
60%+ proceeds; below repairs first, then re-sits.
Every miss gets a named 24-hour repair.
Honest mocks measure; dishonest mocks deceive their maker.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Simulate reality, score honestly, triage misses within a day. The mock's job is diagnosis — let it diagnose.

lessons.title: Entering the Final Examination
lessons.description: What the final demands, how completion and certification work, and staying calm.
objectives: State the final exam rules and completion requirements
Explain how certificates are issued and verified
Apply calm-day tactics for peak performance
lessons.introduction: Twelve modules behind you; one examination ahead. Know the rules, trust the preparation, and walk in calm.

contents.title: Final rules and certification
contents.body: THE FINAL EXAMINATION: 30 questions, 90 minutes, 3 attempts (best counts), 60% pass mark — covering all 12 modules (see the course final exam for the full instructions). COMPLETION requires ALL of: 80%+ lessons finished, 60%+ quiz average, every assignment submitted AND passed, and the final exam passed at 60%+. Certificates are issued AUTOMATICALLY when the system verifies completion — each carries a unique certificate number verifiable on the platform; there is no manual step and no fee beyond the course itself. RESULTS: attempts are graded instantly with explanations for review; after passing, download your certificate from the Certificates page and verify its number. If an attempt fails, the miss-triage from Lesson 1 applies: repair within 24 hours, then use the next attempt — three attempts reward steady improvers.

contents.title: Calm-day tactics
contents.body: NIGHT BEFORE: light review of checklists only (no new material), pack requirements, sleep 7+ hours — sleep consolidates memory; all-night cramming deletes it. EXAM TIME: arrive early, breathe slowly (4 counts in, 6 out) to settle nerves, read ALL instructions first, execute Module 11's two-pass strategy, and trust first instincts on MCQs unless new reasoning emerges (changed answers are wrong more often than right). AFTER: do not post-mortem with friends (it only seeds doubt); review the official explanations when released; celebrate effort whatever the outcome — then repair and re-attempt if needed. You have revised systematically for 12 modules. The final is familiar ground.

contents.title: Worked example: the 60% maths
contents.body: Question: 'I scored 55% on attempt 1. What must change for attempt 2?' Step 1 — Count: 30 questions × 55% ≈ 16–17 correct; passing needs 18+. Step 2 — Triage the ~13 misses by module (e.g. 4 genetics, 3 ecology, 2 practicals, 4 scattered). Step 3 — Repair the CLUSTERS first: 4 genetics misses → 45-minute Module 5 repair (ratios + sex-linkage) converts up to 4 marks; ecology 3 → 30-minute cycles review. Step 4 — Re-attempt after 24 hours: fixing two clusters typically adds 5–7 marks → 70%+. Moral: clustered misses are concentrated gold — mine them first.

contents.title: Key concepts
contents.body:
Final: 30 Qs, 90 min, 3 attempts, 60% pass. Completion: 80% lessons + 60% quiz avg + assignments passed + final passed.
Certificates auto-issue with verifiable unique numbers.
Sleep beats cramming; two passes beat one; clustered misses repair first.

contents.title: Lesson summary
contents.body: Know the thresholds, earn them systematically, and let the system certify real achievement. Calm, sleep and triage carry you the last mile. Good luck — you are ready.

practical.title: Exam-Day Simulation
practical.objective: Rehearse the complete final-exam experience: setup, sitting, review and recovery.
practical.scenario: Tomorrow is the final. Today you run the full simulation and fix the last gaps.
practical.instructions: 1. PREPARE the room exactly as Lesson 1 specifies (desk, timer 40 min, water, phone off). 2. SIT the module mock examination below in one go — no pauses, no notes. 3. MARK immediately and harshly; log every miss (question | concept | reason). 4. REPAIR each miss with a 10-minute targeted re-study (open the named module lesson, write the concept in own words). 5. RE-ATTEMPT all missed questions blind and confirm 100% on the re-attempt. 6. Write a 5-line readiness statement: score, misses, repairs done, re-attempt score, one-line confidence note. SAFETY: take a 10-minute walk between marking and repair — fresh eyes learn faster.
practical.expected_output: Mock score + miss log + repair notes + 100% re-attempt + readiness statement.
evaluation_criteria: Real simulated conditions with honest timing
Every miss logged with concept and reason

assignment.title: Readiness Declaration
assignment.description: Declare final-exam readiness with evidence: scores, repairs and a calm-day plan.
assignment.instructions: Submit: (1) Your mock score with the miss log (question | concept | reason). (2) For EACH miss: the corrected concept in your own words (50+ words each) plus re-attempt result. (3) Your completion checklist status: lessons % done, quiz average, assignments submitted/passed (copy from your dashboard). (4) Your calm-day plan: sleep time, arrival, materials, first-5-minutes routine (100 words). (5) One paragraph on what you will do if attempt 1 fails (triage plan, not panic). 400–500 words plus tables.
assignment.requirements: Evidence must match real dashboard data; declarations without evidence score zero.
assignment.expected_output: Miss repairs + completion status + calm-day plan + contingency paragraph.
evaluation_criteria: Every mock miss repaired accurately in own words
Completion status honestly reported against all four gates
Calm-day and contingency plans specific and realistic

quiz.title: Module 12 Quiz — Final Warmup
quiz.description: Five rapid questions across the whole course.

questions.question: Which row correctly matches test to nutrient?
options: Iodine → starch; Benedict's → reducing sugar; Biuret → protein
questions.explanation: Iodine blackens starch, Benedict's (heated) reddens reducing sugars, biuret purples protein, ethanol emulsifies fats.

questions.question: Meiosis produces:
questions.explanation: Two divisions with one replication: four unique haploid gametes.

questions.question: The main nitrogen-fixing partner of beans is:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium in root nodules fixes N2 to ammonia in exchange for sugars (mutualism).

questions.question: Insulin is released when blood glucose is:
options: High, to lower it by promoting uptake and storage
questions.explanation: High glucose triggers insulin (beta cells): cells absorb glucose, liver stores glycogen. Glucagon reverses lows.

questions.question: A fair test changes:
options: Exactly one independent variable, holding the rest constant
questions.explanation: One IV, fixed controls, measured DV — plus repeats and a control setup for validity.

assessment.title: Module 12 Mock Examination
assessment.description: Full mock examination under real conditions — 10 questions, 40 minutes.
assessment.instructions: ONE sitting, 40 minutes, no notes. Pass mark 60%. This mock simulates the final: same style, same pressure. Triage every miss within 24 hours (see Lesson 1).

questions.question: A dry seed shows no metabolism yet is alive because:
options: It is actually dead until planted
It is dormant — all seven characteristics are potentially present on germination
questions.explanation: Dormancy pauses metabolism; given water/warmth/air, the seed respires, grows and reproduces — alive but waiting.

questions.question: Red blood cells burst in pure water because:
options: Water enters by osmosis and there is no wall to resist pressure
questions.explanation: Osmosis drives water in down its gradient; animal cells lack walls, so they lyse (plant cells would go turgid).

questions.question: The temperature-rate curve for enzymes falls steeply after the optimum due to:
questions.explanation: Heat breaks the weak bonds holding tertiary structure; the active site deforms irreversibly and complexes stop forming.

questions.question: In anaphase I of meiosis:
options: Homologous chromosomes separate, halving the number
questions.explanation: Whole homologues part (reduction division). Chromatids part later in anaphase II.

questions.question: Two brown-eyed carriers (Bb × Bb) have a blue-eyed child with probability:
questions.explanation: Bb × Bb → BB, Bb, Bb, bb: 1 in 4 homozygous recessive (blue).

questions.question: Pesticide resistance in cockroaches evolves because:
options: The pesticide teaches individuals to resist
Pre-existing resistant variants survive and breed
questions.explanation: Selection sorts existing variation: resistant survivors pass alleles on until resistance dominates the population.

questions.question: Eutrophication kills fish mainly through:
options: Fish starving from too much food
questions.explanation: Bloom → die-off → bacterial decay → deoxygenation → suffocation. Oxygen loss is the killer.

questions.question: During inhalation, the diaphragm:
options: Contracts and flattens, expanding chest volume
Pushes air out of the lungs
questions.explanation: Active inhalation: diaphragm flattens + ribs rise → volume up → pressure down → air in.

questions.question: Sugars made in leaves reach the roots via:
options: Phloem translocation from source to sink
Root hairs absorbing them from soil
questions.explanation: Phloem mass flow carries sugars any direction from sources (leaves) to sinks (roots, fruits, tips).

questions.question: A valid investigation of fertiliser on growth must:
options: Vary fertiliser, water and light together
Vary only fertiliser dose, with repeats, controls and fixed water/light
Use one plant per dose with no repeats
questions.explanation: One IV (dose), fixed controls (water, light, species), repeats + means, and a zero-dose control for comparison.
